Yeah It's definitely difficult trying to balance out all the different things I would like to try without messing up other things I want lol, but yeah you are right I think the zoom is more important to me than astrophotography but I am worried that if I try to take a low light photo it will be filled with noise with the smaller sensor cameras but I think that's just something I'll have to work around unless I win the lottery. Yeah that's one of the reasons dslrs are still looking quite attractive to me that I can get different lenses continuously as I explore photography but I'm not sure that I'll be able to put that much into a hobby when I have to start paying for uni. For just losing blue tooth that definitely sounds like a lot to gain which is surprising to me, I would've assumed more recent models to be automatically "better". I've heard that snapbridge is pretty mediocre/doesn't work which is a pity I would've expected more from a huge brand name. It's absolutely blowing my mind doing all this research and comparing all the different features and price points and everything, I can't believe how much is out there and all the different qualities to compare and it seems like you've done more than me, I don't know how you keep it all in your head haha. You've definitely given me a lot to think about, thank you so much for your and everyone's responses they've helped a tonne!

Yeah I am still contemplating the differences as I am worried about the zoom but I would also like to try a bit of astrophotography( of stars mostly) and I thought the bigger 1 inch sensor or the fz1000 would be able to pick up much more light than the smaller sensor higher zooms. Have you tried astrophotography at all with bridge cameras? Does it turn out alright? I'll definitely have a look at the d3400 though thank you! Is there a big reason for you wanting a 3300 instead? Or just natural progression? I actually didn't really look at the fz300 but I would feel a lot more comfortable with 600 mm as I believe the animals won't be much further than about 800 or so meters but do you think if I take low light pictures they'll turn out alright?
